headline: Scotland sees first wild-born beavers in 400 years
meta_description: After four centuries, wild-born beavers have returned to Scotland, marking a remarkable recovery for the species in the region.
summary_short: Scotland has witnessed the birth of wild beavers for the first time in 400 years, signaling a significant ecological milestone.
body:
Scotland has witnessed the birth of wild beavers for the first time in 400 years, marking a remarkable ecological milestone in the country's wildlife recovery.

The return of these animals to Scottish waterways represents a major conservation success. Beavers had vanished from the region centuries ago, but their gradual reestablishment shows how wildlife can reclaim lost ground when conditions improve. This breakthrough demonstrates the potential for species restoration across the UK.

The emergence of wild-born beavers in Scotland reflects years of dedicated conservation effort and changing attitudes toward wildlife management in the region. Their presence enriches river ecosystems and inspires hope for other species facing similar challenges of habitat loss and human pressure.
quick_facts: First wild-born beavers in Scotland in 400 years
Species had disappeared from the region for centuries
Major breakthrough in UK wildlife conservation
